eyebrow: A population of 10,000, sampled 50 at a time
code:
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
orders = pd.Series(rng.gamma(2.0, 30.0, size=10000).round(2))
print("population mean:", round(orders.mean(), 2))

for i in range(3):
    s = orders.sample(50, random_state=i)
    print("sample", i, "mean:", round(s.mean(), 2))
caption: A population is the full group; a sample is the part you actually measured.

code:
population mean: 60.44
sample 0 mean: 60.7
sample 1 mean: 58.77
sample 2 mean: 58.38
caption: Sampling variability: none of the three sample means equals the true 60.44 — nobody made a mistake.
